thread:
sara: Customer ACME reports intermittent streaming 5xx. They see a TCP RST mid-response and billing shows those as server errors — asking for refund on a few calls.

sara: Excerpt from gateway logs:
```
[1725009875.123] conn=12345 id=gw-7 upstream=10.8.2.4:443 -> reset by peer (RST) after 162ms, bytes_sent=3487
[1725009875.124] request_id=abc-123 streaming=true status=5xx classifier=upstream_reset
```

ops-alex: Do we have client-side logs from ACME? Could be their proxy doing an active RST (splice) on idle keepalive. If client initiated, we should not mark as 5xx.

sara: Customer says their infra uses nginx (proxy_pass -> our gateway) and they see a connection closed with `RST` in tcpdump. They insist they didn't call abort.

eng-ryan: Quick hypothesis: nginx is tearing the socket (RST) when it considers the backend dead during half-close; our gateway currently maps upstream RST to 5xx unconditionally if it occurs before full EOF. That will bill as an error.

maya: Can we get a minimal repro? e.g. curl streaming and then kill the client connection to simulate?

sara: Repro they shared (customer):
```bash
# client posts chunked stream then closes socket abruptly
printf "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4\r\ntest\r\n0\r\n\r\n" | nc -q 0 example-gateway 443
# they see RST after last chunk
```

eng-ryan: That matches a client-side abrupt close. Key is ordering: if RST arrives after we flushed final chunk/trailer, treat as client disconnect (non-5xx). If it arrives during chunk body, maybe a network error. We need stronger heuristics.

ops-alex: For mitigation: we can 1) mark these as non-billable while we investigate for specific accounts, 2) add a short window (200ms) where RST following final `0\r\n\r\n` is considered client close, 3) emit better telemetry to correlate socket events to chunk boundaries. Thoughts?

eng-ryan: +1 on telemetry. I'll add an internal flag: `upstream_reset_reason=pre_chunk|post_trailer|unknown` and update billing rule to ignore `post_trailer`. Quick patch might be risky but doable as a config toggle for the gateway group.

sara: Customer wants a refund on 4 calls billed as 5xx today (timestamps provided). Can we treat those specific request IDs as non-billable now?

ops-alex: Yes, ops can backfill billing credits if we confirm they match the reset-post-trailer pattern. Send me the request_ids and I'll queue a credit.

eng-ryan: I'll open ENG issue: #STREAM-987 assign to me. Plan: (a) add socket-chunk correlation logs, (b) implement 200ms post-trailer RST -> classify as client abort, (c) add feature flag to gate behavior, (d) add unit tests and e2e with nginx repro.

sara: Sending request_ids and customer tcpdump to ops.

support-bot: Case logged: ticket#78910 - "ACME streaming RST led to 5xx billing dispute". Ops assigned: ops-alex. ENG issue opened: STREAM-987.

ops-alex: For now I'll queue manual credits for the 4 calls and mark the customer as "investigating - non-billable" so they don't get billed while we roll a fix.

eng-ryan: I'll push the telemetry change to a canary pool and post logs here when available. Thank you all.

sara: Thanks team :heart:
